_note: v14: gated routing between the v6.3 members (v10.3 CLIP + ImageNet-22k ConvNeXt-Base independent CNNs), train/route.py. Instead of one mixing weight over all 333 pairs with gamma deciding seen vs unseen (v6.3), three separate parts: a learned seen/unseen gate (logistic regression on both members' score features, trained on validation: val-seen vs pseudo-unseen images), a seen expert and an unseen expert (each its own mixing weight of the two members, chosen by accuracy inside its branch), combined by hard or soft routing (soft = COSMO, Atzmon & Chechik, CVPR 2019). Motivation (test diagnostic, 2026-11-16): with a perfect gate v5.13 alone would reach HM 75.0% and ConvNeXt alone 81.8% vs 66.3% / 68.6% calibrated, i.e. the seen/unseen decision loses more than either expert. Same members, split (seed 42) and cached validation scores as v6.3, so the comparison is v6.3's validation HM 66.02% on the same images. Decision rule: keep only if validation HM (out-of-fold gate) is > 2 points above the one-weight ensemble on this split. One split only, so treat with the usual ~3-point noise caveat. Not supported by the app (dpd/inference.py) yet.
_result: Not kept: no gain over the one-weight ensemble (v6.3) on the same split. Validation HM 65.61% (out-of-fold gate, hard routing, bias 0.3; seen 76.22%, unseen 57.60%) vs ensemble 66.02% (-0.41). Findings: (1) both experts chose the same mix, weight 0.3 on v10.3 (seen pairs: 90.60% vs v10.3 85.15% / ConvNeXt 90.26%; unseen pairs: 64.35% vs 58.16% / 56.66%), so 'a different model per branch' reduces to the ensemble's single mix; (2) the learned gate does not beat the ensemble's own margin at telling seen from unseen on held-out pairs (AUROC 0.921 vs 0.923; richer feature sets were worse: 0.910 / 0.914, val HM 63.91% / 64.42%), and it puts most of its weight on that margin; (3) the gate is still where the headroom is: a perfect gate with the same experts would give 75.25% on validation. Sanity check: hard routing on the ensemble margin reproduces the ensemble exactly (66.02%). Test (reported, not used to decide): HM 74.98% (seen 64.20%, unseen 90.12%) vs v6.3 74.99%; the gate sent 20.6% of test-seen and 94.9% of test-unseen images to the unseen expert. Top-5 numbers are not comparable with other runs (hard routing ranks only the routed branch's pairs). Follow-up 2026-11-16 (prototype scripts, validation split seed 42 only, not in the repo): three more detector families were tried and none beat the gamma gate. (a) Nearest-neighbour training support in an embedding space (similarity to training images of the best seen pair and of the best unseen pair's crop / disease; v10.3 LoRA, frozen CLIP and BioCLIP embeddings): alone AUROC up to 0.84, added to the margins 63.5-66.1% val HM vs 66.02%. (b) Training-count and shared-crop / shared-disease features: 63.4-65.4%. (c) Margins of four members (v10.3, v5.13, ConvNeXt-Base, ConvNeXt-Base 336) in one gate: AUROC 0.926-0.927, val HM within 0.6 points of the same members' gamma ensemble, never above it by more than 0.6. Detector AUROC stayed at 0.92-0.93 throughout. Why: 89% of misrouted val-seen images were confused with a pseudo-unseen pair of their own crop, and val-seen images whose crop has no pseudo-unseen pair were misrouted only 3% of the time, so seen-vs-unseen is in practice a within-crop disease decision and the gate is limited by cross-crop disease recognition, not by the gate's features. By-product: plain gamma ensembles on this split score 68.25% (0.2 v5.13 + 0.8 ConvNeXt-Base 336) and 68.66% (0.2 v5.13 + 0.3 ConvNeXt-Base + 0.5 ConvNeXt-Base 336), found by an exploratory weight search and not yet run as configs.
title: gated_router

router._note: weight_grid: weight on the first member (v10.3) for each expert, 0 = ConvNeXt alone, 1 = v10.3 alone. gate: L2 logistic regression (C), class-balanced; validation HM uses out-of-fold gate predictions with cv_folds folds grouped by pair. bias_grid: shift added to the gate logit (the routing threshold), chosen on validation with the mode.

gate._note: features: which score features the gate sees (train/route.py gate_features). Compared on validation (out-of-fold gate): 'members' 63.91%, 'members+mix' 64.42%, 'margins' 65.61%; fewer features generalise better to pairs the gate was not trained on, so 'margins' is used.

validation._note: Same split procedure, seed and settings as v6.3. gamma_grid is only used for the baselines printed for comparison (members alone and the one-weight ensemble, as train/ensemble.py); the router itself has no gamma. reuse_val_scores_from: folders whose cached member validation scores (same split) are reused instead of retraining.
